description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: Add session continuity between developer and validator agents
items.intent: The validator must have full context of what the developer did and why — continuing the session eliminates cold-start context reconstruction from diffs and produces dramatically better validation verdicts.
items.description: Each agent currently starts a fresh Claude session. The validator has to re-discover everything by reading git diffs. If the developer's session ID is captured and passed to the validator via --continue/--session-id, the validator inherits the full implementation context. Implementation: capture session_id from developer's --output-format json output, store it, pass to validator invocation. Requires switching to --output-format json in run_agent_process() or extracting session_id from claude's output.
steps: In run_agent_process(), switch default output format to json when no AGENT_OUTPUT_FILE is set
After developer agent completes, extract and store session_id from json output
Before validator invocation, set AGENT_SESSION_ID to the developer's session_id and add --continue flag
Ensure session continuity is opt-out (add config key to disable if needed)
Test that validator receives implementation context without needing to re-read diffs

acceptanceCriteria.text: Developer agent output is parsed as JSON to extract session_id
Validator invocation uses --continue or --session-id from developer session

items.title: Add per-sprint cost tracking via --output-format json
items.intent: Every sprint must report its token usage and estimated cost — without visibility into per-sprint costs, autonomous run-done sessions can burn through budgets silently.
items.description: run_agent_process() currently uses --output-format text, discarding token usage metadata. Switch to --output-format json and extract usage.input_tokens + usage.output_tokens from each agent invocation. Accumulate per-sprint and per-session totals. Report in session summary and archive entry (sprints.jsonl).
steps: In run_agent_process(), use --output-format json (when not using --print) and parse the JSON result
Extract usage.input_tokens and usage.output_tokens from each agent run
Accumulate token counts per sprint (developer + validator) and per session
Add token counts to the sprint archive entry in sprints.jsonl
Display token summary in the end-of-session report

acceptanceCriteria.text: Agent runs produce JSON output that includes token usage
Sprint archive entries include token usage
Session summary reports total tokens used

items.title: Add --bare flag to all agent invocations
items.intent: Every agent invocation must be reproducible across machines — no local hooks, MCP servers, skills, or auto-memory leaking into orchestrated agents.
items.description: run_agent_process() spawns claude without --bare. Agents pick up local config that differs between environments. Add --bare to the claude_args array in run_agent_process().
steps: In run_agent_process(), add '--bare' to the claude_args array after the initial declaration
Verify the orchestrator still passes CLAUDE.md content explicitly via -p prompt injection
Update checksums.sha256 if the main script changes

acceptanceCriteria.text: CLAUDE.md content is still loaded and injected into agent prompts

items.title: Clarify developer scope rule for entry-point wiring
items.intent: The developer must know exactly when wiring to entry points is in-scope — ambiguity causes retry loops when the validator rejects either interpretation.
items.description: developer.md says 'implement ONLY your assigned item' but also 'wire to real entry points.' Add explicit guidance that entry-point wiring is always in-scope.
steps: In developer.md, add clarifying paragraph: entry-point wiring necessary for integration is in-scope
In validator.md, clarify scope violations for wiring are acceptable

acceptanceCriteria.text: Developer prompt clarifies entry-point wiring is always in-scope

items.title: Resolve circular scaffolding gate dependency between groomer and architect
items.intent: Scaffolding detection must run before readiness gating — the groomer cannot gate on missing scaffolding if the architect hasn't created the items yet.
items.description: Groomer blocks feature readiness if scaffolding is missing, but Architect creates scaffolding items. Add explicit guidance that gating only applies to existing scaffolding items.
steps: In groomer.md, clarify scaffolding gating applies to existing items only

acceptanceCriteria.text: Groomer prompt clarifies scaffolding gating applies to existing items

items.title: Add notification command exit code capture and stderr logging
items.intent: Notification failures must be diagnosable — suppressing stderr and reporting the wrong exit code makes webhook debugging impossible.
items.description: NOTIFY_CMD execution suppresses stderr and the warning references wrong $?. Capture exit code immediately and log stderr to sprint log.
steps: Capture exit code: local rc=$? immediately after bash -c
Redirect stderr to sprint log instead of /dev/null

items.title: Quote _HASH_CMD variable in cmd-update.sh
items.intent: The hash command must work regardless of path — unquoted command variables break when paths contain spaces.
items.description: cmd-update.sh uses $_HASH_CMD unquoted. Quote it to prevent word splitting.
steps: Quote all uses of $_HASH_CMD in cmd-update.sh

items.title: Add groomer populate mode trigger clarity
items.intent: The groomer must know when to use Populate Mode vs normal grooming — without a trigger, it may populate a non-empty backlog or groom an empty one.
items.description: groomer.md has both modes but no guidance on when each applies. Add conditional: Populate Mode when PRD attached and backlog near-empty, otherwise normal grooming.
steps: Add explicit criteria for Populate Mode vs normal grooming to groomer.md

acceptanceCriteria.text: Groomer prompt has criteria for mode selection

items.title: Strengthen integration check enforcement via orchestrator runtime injection
items.intent: The validator's integration check must be context-sensitive — hard-fail when the item's intent involves wiring or integration, advisory otherwise. This closes the fragment gap identified in PR #21 without rewriting agent prompts.
steps: In build_agent_prompt() validator section, strengthen the runtime integration-check injection to escalate from advisory to hard-fail when the item intent contains integration-related keywords (wire, integrate, connect, entry point, endpoint)
Add a runtime injection line instructing the validator to FAIL (not just advise) when integration keywords are present in intent and code is disconnected
Update checksums.sha256 after modifying the orchestrator

acceptanceCriteria.text: Orchestrator runtime injection includes integration hard-fail for integration-scoped items
Integration check remains advisory for items without integration intent
